title: Check one access against the slice rule

hints: e is the sum of the terms, so its lowest value is the sum of the low ends and its highest is the sum of the high ends.
Two tests, as in lesson 2.3: the low end must be at least 0, and the high end plus size must be at most s.
lo = sum(l for l, _ in terms), and the same for hi. Return lo >= 0 and hi + size <= s.
explain: Bound each term of e on its own, then add the low ends and add the high ends. The access stays in iteration r's slice when the lowest e is at least 0 and the highest e plus the access size is at most S. It is the bounds proof from lesson 2.3, with the slice standing in for the whole buffer.
